claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and all relevant equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets can be prepared as homogeneous, single-phase FCC materials by thermomechanical processing.
The controlled comparison should vary Mn inclusion or exclusion while keeping thermomechanical processing and the other alloying elements constant.
The proposed behavior applies under ambient-temperature, quasi-static to moderate-strain-rate deformation.
Mn impedes a dislocation-triggered FCC-to-HCP transformation in these alloys.
The FCC-to-HCP transformation is magnetically tunable.
Mn-free or Mn-diluted quaternary and ternary subsets generally facilitate the FCC-to-HCP transformation at deformation-induced defects.
The relevant structural mediator consists of nanoscale HCP regions or twins/lamellae nucleated at dislocation intersections and internal boundaries.
Magnetically frustrated Mn eliminates or minimizes the energy difference between FCC and HCP configurations.
The Mn-associated magnetic state suppresses HCP nucleation at dislocation intersections.
Removing or diluting Mn reduces magnetic frustration and lowers the kinetic barrier for dislocation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation provides a secondary work-hardening mechanism.
The transformation delays yielding and raises yield strength.
Mn-free quaternary and ternary subsets will develop more deformation-induced HCP than the quinary baseline.
Mn-free quaternary and ternary subsets will have higher work-hardening rates than the quinary baseline.
Mn-free quaternary and ternary subsets will have higher yield strengths than the quinary baseline.
The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy will form less HCP and exhibit a lower work-hardening response than the Mn-free subsets.
The proposed relationship is limited to initially single-phase FCC materials and testing conditions where dislocation slip and transformation-induced mechanisms are operative.
Quantitative property and phase-transformation differences may depend on grain size, processing history, and testing conditions.
Other magnetic interactions and stacking-fault-energy variations may affect the observed outcomes.

contradictions.description: Removing Mn while retaining equiatomic compositions necessarily changes the atomic fractions of the remaining elements, and forming a ternary subset requires removing at least one additional element. Thus the instruction to hold all other alloying elements constant is incompatible with the stated equiatomic quaternary/ternary comparison unless 'constant' refers only to element identities or processing rather than concentrations.
